summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would set a minimum price for milk paid to farmers and create a mandatory code of conduct for the dairy industry.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission would be required to determine the base price for milk fat and protein content, and a new offence would apply to processors buying milk below that price.
The bill would also require the Productivity Commission to review the price-setting amendments and consider whether a divestiture regime for the food and grocery industries should be introduced.
changes: The ACCC would establish a minimum price for milk fat and protein content.
A mandatory code of conduct would regulate the relationship between dairy farmers and processors.
The relevant Minister would refer an inquiry to the Productivity Commission.
A processor that agrees to buy milk for less than the base price would commit an offence.
The Productivity Commission would hold hearings and report on the effectiveness of the price amendments.
The Minister could not end the Productivity Commission inquiry before the report is submitted.
summary.affected: Dairy farmers, milk processors, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, and the Productivity Commission.
